subject: Post-call: Isolated deployment discovery + outstanding asks
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@meditrust.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Isolated deployment discovery + outstanding asks

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our end and the concrete asks so your network/security and procurement teams can triage. I tried to keep this tight.

Summary of pain & goals (as we heard them)
- Regulatory driver: EU patient data must remain in-country and never egress Meditrust networks.
- Air-gapped requirement for certain workloads: ability to run inference in an isolated VLAN/segment with no outbound internet except through an approved jump host.
- Goal: replace an aging on-prem rules engine with LLM-based triage for inbound patient intake while preserving auditability and retention controls.
- Timeline: procurement window targets Q1 2027 pilot, enterprise rollout H2 2027.

Technical constraints noted
1) No outbound egress from core network except outbound via a hardened bastion (jump host) managed by Meditrust.
2) Hardware: customer prefers certified rack with at least 2x A100-class GPUs or equivalent on Azure Stack (they also mentioned potential on-prem racks).
3) KMS requirement: customer-managed keys preferred (HSM/KMS) for model weights + logs.
4) Installation: on-site deployment may be required for initial model loading if remote download is not allowed.

Open questions / asks for your team (please answer inline where possible)
A. Network: can you share a network diagram or a short list of egress controls and jump-host procedures? (ports allowed, IP ranges, jump-host auth method)
B. Data flows: will patient PII ever leave the isolated subnet for backups or analytics? If yes, what controls are expected?
C. Procurement: any standard on-prem licensing terms or contract clauses we should pre-clear (NDA already signed—thanks)?
D. Installation: do you require vendor personnel onsite for model load and initial testing, or is an offline transfer (encrypted HDD) acceptable?

Next steps I propose
- We’ll circulate an initial isolation checklist (attached) and a short deployment proposal for your review by Tue 24 Nov.
- Marcus will scope an install plan and estimate for on-site assist if needed.
- Grace will draft a short note on HSM/KMS options we support and the SLA delta for private instances.

Attachments: redwood-private-one-pager.pdf, isolation-checklist.xlsx (attached)

If you want, we can schedule a short follow-up (30m) next week with your network/security folks to walk through the diagram. Happy to adapt to whatever format helps the team.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0173

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@meditrust.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Meditrust Legal <legal@meditrust.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Isolated deployment discovery + outstanding asks

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers below; I’ve copied Legal for visibility.

A. Network: we can share a simplified network diagram. Allowed outbound is only to our jump-host (10.12.0.5) and a narrow set of IP ranges for vendor management (we will provide the CIDR blocks). Only SSH (port 22) and an approved HTTPS egress proxy (443) are allowed via jump-host. Auth is via our corporate SSO + short-lived certificates.
B. Data flows: patient PII must not leave the isolated subnet. Aggregated, de-identified telemetry can be routed out nightly to analytics; that will be a separate project with DPO sign-off.
C. Procurement: our procurement team will need a copy of standard terms; we have a few mandatory clauses (data residency, indemnity caps). Procurement contact is sara.klein@meditrust.com.
D. Installation: offline model load is preferred for the pilot (encrypted HDD or physically delivered disk). On-site vendor personnel may be allowed for final cutover but will need background checks and limited network access.

We’ll try to get the network diagram to you by Wed 25 Nov. In the meantime, please send the checklist and a rough SOW so procurement can budget.

—Alicia
Alicia Torres | Head of IT Infrastructure | Meditrust Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@meditrust.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Isolated deployment discovery + outstanding asks

Alicia — appreciated. Attached is a first-pass deployment proposal and the isolation checklist filled with the items we discussed. Highlights:
- We can support offline model delivery (encrypted .tar on FDE HDD) and on-site engineer for secure load. Marcus, can you confirm a 2-day on-site window for model loading + validation in the pilot?
- For KMS/HSM: Grace has outlined two options (bring-your-own HSM via PKCS#11 or Redwood-managed HSM kept inside the isolated network using customer-owned key material).
- SOW: I included a budget placeholder for hardware validation and 2 days of on-site support. This is intentionally light pending your procurement/Ops input.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRDW-2026-0892-deployment-plan (proposal + checklist)

Marcus — if an on-site load is needed, we’ll need arrival window, required security paperwork, and the permitted network ports to pre-configure.

Alicia — if you want, I can schedule a 30-min call on Thu to run procurement through the SOW.

Thanks — Jordan

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 07:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Isolated deployment discovery + outstanding asks

Jordan — looping in a couple of quick legal questions so we can flag them to procurement:
1) Encryption at rest: we need confirmation that customer-managed keys (HSM) are supported and that Redwood will not have persistent access to plaintext model artifacts.
2) Audit logs: will Redwood provide tamper-evident audit logs of inference requests and admin actions for the private instance? Retention policy expected: 7 years for audit trails.
3) Data deletion: process for certifying deletion of models and logs at contract termination.

Please respond to each point; procurement expects these answers before accepting the SOW into their pipeline.

Regards,
Meditrust Legal
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Legal Qs + HSM notes (for response)

Internal note — Jordan / Marcus: draft replies to Legal below (I’ll paste into an email once you sign off):
1) Encryption at rest: we support customer-managed keys via HSM (PKCS#11) and can confirm Redwood will not retain plaintext copies of customer model artifacts. We’ll include a technical appendix describing key lifecycle and where keys are stored.
2) Audit logs: we can enable immutable audit logging (WORM-like store) inside the private instance. Retention configurable up to 7 years; costs vary with retention length.
3) Data deletion: we’ll provide documented procedures for secure wipe of model artifacts, logs, and a signed attestation at termination. If physical media used for initial model transfer is provided by Redwood, it will be cryptographically wiped or returned per Meditrust policy.

Marcus — can you confirm the on-site engineer checklist items (background check lead time, required credentials) so I can include them in the response?

Grace
Head of Product Ops | Redwood Inference
